summary: CC load_value/store_value had no 16-bit case, so a uint16_t store (p[i] = inw(...)) emitted a 4-byte mov [ecx], eax, doubling every write into the ATA sector buffer and corrupting kernel memory.
evidence: `p[i] = inw(...)` where `p` is `uint16_t*` generates `mov [ecx], eax` (a 4-byte store) instead of a 2-byte store

summary: AS had no 32-bit-mode mov r16, r/m16 / mov r/m16, r16 memory forms (e.g. mov ax,[eax] / mov [ecx],ax), which the new 16-bit codegen needed.
evidence: Let me add the 32-bit-mode `mov r16, m16` / `mov m16, r16` forms right after the register-to-register 16-bit form

summary: AS encoded movzx r32, r16 (register form) with a spurious 0x66 prefix, turning movzx eax,ax into movzx ax,ax so the upper 16 bits were never cleared.
evidence: `movzx eax, ax` (register-to-register form) incorrectly emits a `0x66` operand-size prefix, turning it into `movzx ax, ax` (a no-op)

summary: AS encoded in ax,dx (and out dx,ax) without the 0x66 operand-size prefix, so each inw read 32 bits from the ATA data port, dropping every other word and making tinyfs mount fail (bad superblock magic).
evidence: `in ax, dx` is missing its `0x66` operand-size prefix — it's encoding a 32-bit `in eax, dx` instead, which reads **two words** from the ATA data port per call

summary: CC never inferred array_len for a global `T name[] = {...}`, so sizeof(lower_table) was 0, TABLE_LEN was 0 and keyboard_getchar discarded every scancode, leaving the shell with no keyboard input.
evidence: Our parser never computes the actual length for `[]` (leaves `array_len = -1`), so `sizeof(lower_table)` evaluates to 0

summary: The array-size inference fix only covered globals; function-local `static const T ops[] = {...}` (script parser operator tables) still got size 0.
evidence: these are `static` *local* array declarations with inferred size, a case my earlier fix (scoped to globals only) didn't cover

summary: Block comments in the new t12 regression test (and the matching parser.c comment) contained the path kernel/lang/*/parser.c, whose `*/` closed the comment early so CC failed to parse the test.
evidence: My comment text contained a literal `*/` sequence, prematurely closing the C block comment.

summary: qemu_type.py's keymap has no mapping for '(' and similar characters, so ad-hoc scripts with call syntax could not be typed into the shell for diagnosis.
evidence: ValueError: qemu_type: no key mapping for '('

summary: CC had no struct/union by-value assignment: `*p = save;` copied only 4 bytes of parser_t, corrupting the script parser's backtracking state ('script: parse error: unexpected token').
evidence: struct-by-value assignment/copy isn't supported at all — ... silently copying just 4 bytes of a ~90+ byte `parser_t` struct

summary: CC did not support struct-returning functions (no hidden-pointer ABI), so eval.c's mkint()/mkstr() value constructors returned garbage and `run hello.tsh` printed '2 2' in an endless loop.
evidence: This requires implementing struct-by-value function returns (the classic "hidden pointer" ABI pattern)

summary: CC passed struct/union parameters as a flat 4 bytes instead of copying the whole struct onto the stack (used by print_value(value_t v)).
AS fixed limits (MAX_STMTS 4096, MAX_SYMS 512, MAX_RELOCS 256) were too small for the larger struct-copy codegen output of eval.c, aborting the build.
evidence:
as: too many statements
make: *** [Makefile:108: build/lang/script/eval.o] Error 1

summary: CC's read_escape had no case for \b (or \f, \v, \a), so '\b' lexed to the letter 'b' and every typed 'b' in the shell was treated as a backspace ('build' arrived as 'uild').
evidence: `read_escape` doesn't handle `\b` (backspace) at all, so it falls through to the `default: return c;` case, returning the literal letter `'b'`
